name: exposure_pilot
purpose: Estimate block-level variance, runtime, failure rate, and assay sensitivity for the matched ConvLSTM trajectory-reuse experiment without revealing effect locations.

nearby.construction: independently simulated reservoir events selected by state-distance quantile band; each reservoir event used once

arms.B: 64 independent replacement trajectories under fresh appearances
arms.C: 64 evaluation-source trajectories under appearances distinct from the evaluation render
arms.D: 64 independently simulated reservoir events, one per source, whose RMS state distance to that source lies between the 0.1st and 1st percentiles of independent-pair distances
arms.E: the exact 64 renders in the exact population (diagnostic reference, not a ceiling)

populations.source: one held-out render per source trajectory, unseen by every arm
populations.exact: the render E trains on; unseen by B, C, and D
populations.independent: 128 independently sampled trajectories under fresh appearances

primary_metric: mean Euclidean center error over the 16 future frames
blinding: Only dispersion, runtime, balance checks, and a binary exact-render positive-control check are reported. Contrast means remain unreported until the effect threshold is frozen.
positive_control: E exact-population gain over B is positive in at least 75% of blocks
claim_boundary: Discarded feasibility blocks. No effect estimate from this run may be reported as evidence of trajectory reuse.
supersedes: Version 1 engineering run used source-perturbed nearby events and evaluated E only on its trained renders; preserved as results/exposure_pilot_v1_engineering_blinded.json
